Nate: Hey Joanna, check this out! I won my fourth video game tournament on Friday! It was awesome competing and showing off my skills - and the victory was indescribable. I'm really proud that I can make money doing what I love. This one was online!
Joanna: Congrats, Nate! That's awesome! So proud of you. Your hard work really paid off - keep it up! BTW, I took a road trip for research for my next movie while you were winning. Much-needed break and a chance to explore new places and get inspired.
Nate: Thanks, Joanna! Your support means a lot to me. That road trip sounds great! Where did you go? Did you discover any interesting places?
Joanna: Thanks Nate! Appreciate your kind words. I went to Woodhaven, a small town in the Midwest. Got to see some lovely scenery and historic buildings. Checked out the library there, it had a cool old book collection!
Nate: That place looks interesting! Did you find any cool books there?
Joanna: I stumbled upon this super cool book from the 1900s with stories and sketches - so awesome to read about the town and the people living there!
Nate: That sounds really interesting! Anyting specific stick out to you about it?
Joanna: Woodhaven has had an interesting past with lots of cool people. Seeing how much it changed sparked ideas for my next script.
Nate: Real-life stories are the best for inspiration. Can't wait to hear about your next one. Keep it up!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! I'm stoked about this new script. It's different from my previous work, but it has the potential to be something awesome! I'll be sure to keep you posted.
Nate: I'm sure it will do just as well as your last one! Keep on trying and believe in yourself!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! Your encouragement really means a lot to me. You're the best for supporting me in my writing journey.
Nate: I'm always here for you! You've got so much talent, just keep going for it!
Joanna: I will! I actually started on a book recently since my movie did well!
Nate: Nice! I'm curious, what is it about?
Joanna: That page specifically has some dialogues exploring loss, redemption, and forgiveness. It's a deep and emotional story that I'm really excited about!
Nate: Wow, Joanna! It sounds awesome. I'm so excited to see how it all plays out!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! I'm so glad you're excited. I've never really tried publishing a book, but this might be the first!
Nate: Good luck on that! I'm sure people will recognise you as the same author of the movie you got published and love the book even more.
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! Your belief in me means a lot. I'll keep doing my best. Thanks for the support!
Nate: No problem, Joanna. I'm here for you. Your hard work will pay off, I promise. Believe in yourself and your talent - you're incredible!

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
